title: Article 137 — Review of judgments or orders by the Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 137 provides that, subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament or any rules made under Article 145, the Supreme Court shall have power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.
content.glance: SC may review its own judgments/orders, subject to parliamentary law and Art 145 rules.
content.study:
Article 137 confers review jurisdiction on the Supreme Court over its own judgments and orders. Exercise is subject to parliamentary law and rules under Article 145. Review is not an appeal; grounds are limited (e.g. error apparent on the face of the record) as developed in practice and rules.

Examination: power to review own decisions; subject to law and Art 145 rules; distinct from appeal/SLP.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Subject to parliamentary law and rules under Article 145, the Supreme Court has power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can the Supreme Court review its own judgments?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. Under Article 137, subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament or any rules made under Article 145, the Supreme Court has power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.

examTips: Review of own judgments; subject to law and Art 145 rules.

keyTakeaways: Art 137: SC power to review its judgments and orders.
